subject: question about variance-covariance matrix specification for multiple year n-mixture model

messages.author: 30210ed812ebcdc5
messages.subject: question about variance-covariance matrix specification for multiple year n-mixture model
parts:
Hi,

I am interested in implementing the static binomial N-Mixture model with few species and symmetric interactions for joint models for abundance to assess interactions among species abundance. Section 8.5.1 on the AHME 2 (page 509). The code on the book example is this:

  # Specify MVN prior for random site effects in lambda for each species
  for (i in 1:nsites){
    eta.lam[i,1:nspec] ~ dmnorm(mu.eta[1:nspec], Omega[1:nspec,1:nspec])
  }
  for (k in 1:nspec){
    mu.eta[k] <- 0
  }
  # Vague inverse Wishart prior for variance-covariance matrix
  Omega[1:nspec,1:nspec] ~ dwish(R[1:nspec,1:nspec], df)
  Sigma2[1:nspec,1:nspec] <- inverse(Omega[1:nspec,1:nspec])
  # Scale var/covar matrix to become the correlation matrix
  for (i in 1:nspec){
    for (k in 1:nspec){
      rho[i,k] <- Sigma2[i,k] / (sqrt(Sigma2[i,i]) * sqrt(Sigma2[k,k]))
    }
  }

The difference is that I have multiple years of data which I am treating as a random effect. My question is: Is it okay to run that section of the code on a loop for each year? Or do you need to specify hyperpriors on Omega (I do not see how to do that)? Something like this:

  # Specify MVN prior for random site effects in lambda for each species and for year year
for (t in 1:nYears){
  for (j in 1:nsites){
        eta.lam[j,1:nspec,t] ~ dmnorm(mu.eta[1:nspec,t], Omega[1:nspec,1:nspec,t])
  } #j

  for (s in 1:nspec){
    mu.eta[s,t] <- 0
  }

  # Vague inverse Wishart prior for variance-covariance matrix
  Omega[1:nspec,1:nspec,t] ~ dwish(R[1:nspec,1:nspec,t], df)
  Sigma2[1:nspec,1:nspec,t] <- inverse(Omega[1:nspec,1:nspec,t])

  #Scale var/covar matrix to become the correlation matrix
  for(i in 1:nspec){
    for (k in 1:nspec){
        rhocor[i,k,t] <- Sigma2[i,k,t] / (sqrt(Sigma2[i,i,t]) * sqrt(Sigma2[k,k,t]))
    } #k
  } #s
}#t

I did run a test and the model seems to be working, but I am not sure if estimating a variance-covariance for each year is appropriate. 

I will highly appreciate any insight into this. And I apologize if the information I provided is not enough, I can provide more details if needed.

Thank you very much

Ramiro

messages.subject: Re: question about variance-covariance matrix specification for multiple year n-mixture model
parts:
Hey Ramiro,

Just thinking out loud here. Currently you're estimating the covariances separately for each year, even though you might want to model the sigmas and rhos in Sigma <- diag(sigma) %*% Rho %*% diag(sigma) hierarchically, right?

This will be a pain if you have many species, but you could do something like:

Omega[1:nspec,1:nspec,t]<- inverse(Sigma2[1:nspec,1:nspec,t])  # covariance to precision matrix
Sigma2[1:nspec,1:nspec,t] <- diag(sigma[1:nspec,t]) %*% Rho[1:nspec,1:nspec,t] %*% diag(sigma[1:nspec,t])  # decompose covariance into sigmas and Rho
## define Rho somewhere; this'll be a pain depending on how many species there are, but something like
Rho[1,1,t] <- 1
Rho[1,2,t] <- rho[1,t]
Rho[1,3,t] <- rho[1,t] * rho[2,t]  # not even sure if this would be the correct cell entry, but you get where I'm going?

# hierarchical sigmas (log-transformed)

log(sigma[s,t]) ~ dnorm(sigma_mu[s], sigma_tau[s])
}

# hierarchical rho's
for (j in 1:nrho) {
   rho[j,t] <- (exp(2 * rho_fz) - 1) / (exp(2 * rho_fz) + 1)  # need to do inverse Fisher's z-transform to go from [-∞,∞] back to [-1,1]
   rho_fz[j,t] ~ dnorm(rho_fz_mu[j], rho_fz_tau[j])  # need to do the random year effects on unbounded scale (Fisher's z-transform)
}

and then place priors on sigma_mu[1:nspec], sigma_tau[1:nspec], rho_fz_mu[1:nrho], and rho_fz_tau[1:nrho].

Cheers,

Matt
